beliefs: f reverses the order of characters in the string [E1]
f then swaps the case of each letter (upper<->lower), leaving non-letters unchanged [E1, E3]
The case swap is applied to the reversed string, not the original [E3]
The first output character is the case-swapped last input character shifted back by 2 alphabetically within its own case (a->y, A->Y, wrapping z->x, Z->X) [E4, E5, E6, E11]
Non-ASCII Latin-1 letters are case-swapped and shifted back by 2 within their contiguous letter block, skipping the ×/÷ gaps [E12, E13]
The -2 shift applies only when the last character is a letter; otherwise the first output char is just the reversed last char [E8, E9]

The lowercase Latin-1 block is 0xE0..0xFE excluding ÷(0xF7), and à(0xE0) wraps to Þ(0xDE), á(0xE1) to ß(0xDF), ß(0xDF) to Ý(0xDD) — so the wrap base is 0xDE, extending the block down to Þ [E14, E21, E22]
The uppercase Latin-1 block is 0xC0..0xDE excluding ×(0xD7), and À(0xC0) wraps to ¾(0xBE), Á(0xC1) to ¿(0xBF) — so the wrap base is 0xBE, extending the block down to ¾ [E16, E19]
The uppercase block's -2 shift is plain codepoint-2 skipping × (Ñ→Ï, Ó→Ñ, Ö→Ò, Ø→Ö, Þ→Ü), consistent with the 0xBE-based block [E19, E20]
The lowercase block's -2 shift is plain codepoint-2 skipping ÷ (á→ß, à→Þ, ÿ→ý), consistent with the 0xDE-based block [E21, E22]
notes: Fixed the lowercase block base from 0xDF to 0xDE (so ß→Ý and à→Þ), matching E22's observed à→Þ and ß→Ý. Also fixed the uppercase block to plain codepoint-2 skipping × rather than 0xBE-block indexing, per E19/E20.
